bib.title: LLaMA-Adapter V2: Parameter-Efficient Visual Instruction Model

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "LLaMA-Adapter V2: Parameter-Efficient Visual Instruction Model". Authors: Peng Gao, Jiaming Han, Renrui Zhang, Ziyi Lin, Shijie Geng, Aojun Zhou, Wei Zhang, Pan Lu, Conghui He, Xiangyu Yue, Hongsheng Li, Yu Qiao. Shanghai AI Laboratory, CUHK MMLab and Rutgers. Preprint, arXiv:2304.15010v1, 28 Apr 2023.
PDF: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/08-multimodal-engineering/sources/gao-2023-llama-adapter-v2.pdf

COVERAGE: I read all 67,388 characters. That covers 15 pages: the body, Tables 1 to 3, the Figure 1 to 11 captions and the full reference list. The paper has no appendix. I skimmed the long sample outputs in Table 2 and Figures 6 to 9 for any claims they make. Figures 10 and 11 are images with no extractable text, so only their captions came through.

ANSWER TO THE SPECIFIC QUESTION: The 13B figure for MiniGPT-4 and LLaVA appears in one place only: **Table 1, "Training Comparison of Different Methods", page 3**, in its last column, "Tuning Parameters Size". The rows are quoted verbatim below. The table note says how they counted: "we count all the data and tuning parameters needed to convert the pretrained vision model and LLM into a visual instruction model." The prose never says MiniGPT-4 tunes 13B. It actually says something different: "MiniGPT-4 connects a frozen visual encoder and an LLM by pre-training on 134 million image-text pairs" (p.2). It then contrasts LLaVA with it: "Different from MiniGPT-4, LLaV A fine-tunes the whole LLM". So the paper's own text implies MiniGPT-4 does not tune the LLM, which conflicts with the 13B in its table. If the note says MiniGPT-4 tunes 13B, cite it as "per the authors' Table 1 count", or drop MiniGPT-4 from that clause. The only other 13B mention is in the Figure 5 caption, and it is about Vicuna.

VERDICT ON THE NOTE'S FOUR CLAIMS:
(1) "14M vs 13B": confirmed in Table 1. The MiniGPT-4 figure carries the caveat above.
(2) "LLaMA stays frozen except its norms": broadly confirmed. Precisely, the norms are unfrozen and each linear layer gets a new bias and scale; all other LLaMA weights stay frozen.
(3) The joint-training split: confirmed verbatim in Sec 4.2. Caption data trains "visual projection layers and early zero-initialized attention with gating". Instruction data trains "late adaptation prompts together with zero gating, the unfrozen norm, newly added bias and scale factors (or optional low-rank adaption)".
(4) "Lags LLaVA on quality": the paper says "lags behind LLaVA in terms of visual understanding capability". That is narrower than "quality", and the paper gives no number for the gap.

  number: 14M

  quote: "can perform open-ended multi-modal instructions by merely introducing 14M parameters over LLaMA"
  where: p.1, abstract
- claim: The bias, scale and norm parameters alone are about 0.04% of LLaMA, roughly 5M. The other parameters (adapters, projection, early attention) make up the rest of the 14M, but the paper never breaks that down.
  number: 0.04%, ~5M

  quote: "the number of newly added parameters only accounts for 0.04% (∼5M) of the entire LLaMA"
  where: p.5, Sec 4.1

  number: none

  quote: "All the parameters in normalization layers, linear layer bias and scale are set to be updated during training, while the remaining parameters in LLaMA are kept frozen."
  where: p.8, Implementation Details. The method is also given on p.5: "we first unfreeze all the normalization layers in LLaMA. For each linear layer in the Transformer, we add a bias and a scale factor as two learnable parameters."

  number: 500K vs 50K, the data imbalance that motivates the split

  where: p.5-6, Sec 4.2. The imbalance is stated as "data volume difference between 500K image-text pairs and 50K instruction data".

  number: 80M; 7B-65B

LIMITS:
- No compute is reported anywhere: no GPUs, hours, epochs, learning rate or batch size.
- The visual instruction model is never scored on a benchmark. The evidence is qualitative examples (Figures 6 to 9) plus COCO captioning in Table 3.
- There is no head-to-head comparison with LLaVA or MiniGPT-4. "Lags behind LLaVA" is the authors' own admission, with no number behind it.
- The only GPT-4 judging covers the text-only 65B chatbot, with ChatGPT as the reference. The visual model was not judged by GPT-4.
- Table 1 does not say which LLaMA size the visual model uses. The implementation details give 7B.
- The 14M is never broken down by component.
- V1 preprint from April 2023. The baselines (LLaVA v1, MiniGPT-4, ChatGPT, Vicuna) have dated.
- The future work the authors list is fine-tuning on multimodal instruction data, or with LoRA.

BUILDS ON:
- LLaMA-Adapter, Zhang et al. 2023 [72]: zero-init attention and gating, the base method.
- LLaMA, Touvron et al. 2023 [63].
- BitFit, Ben Zaken et al. 2021 [70], and SSF, Lian et al. 2022 [36], which the authors name as similar to their bias tuning.
- LoRA, Hu et al. 2021/2022 [25, 26].
- GPT-4-LLM (Instruction tuning with GPT-4), Peng et al. 2023 [50], the instruction data.
- COCO Captions, Chen et al. 2015 [6].
- CLIP, Radford et al. 2021 [52], the visual encoder.
- ShareGPT [1], and Vicuna, Chiang et al. 2023 [7], for the 80 evaluation questions.
- The baselines: LLaVA, Liu et al. 2023 [38], and MiniGPT-4, Zhu et al. 2023 [78].
- The caption baselines: ClipCap, Mokady et al. 2021 [46]; BLIP, Li et al. 2022 [33]; BLIP-2, Li et al. 2023 [32].

CODE: Eq. 1 and 2 on p.5: `y = W· x → y = s· (W· x + b), (1)  where b = Init(0), s = Init(1). (2)`. That is the whole bias-tuning method. Table 2's regex examples are not worth keeping.

FIGURES:
- Figure 2 (p.5), "Joint Training Paradigm in LLaMA-Adapter V2. We utilize both image-text caption and language-only instruction data to jointly train LLaMA-Adapter V2, optimizing disjoint groups of learnable parameters." It shows which parameters each data type trains: projection plus early attention for captions, norm/scale/bias plus late attention for instructions, everything else frozen. This is the direct visual for "Which layers you reached".
- Figure 3 (p.6), "Early Fusion of Visual Knowledge. Following LLaMA-Adapter, we insert static adaptation prompts into the last L layers. For visual prompts, we insert them in the early stage of LLM, disjointing with adaptation prompts." It contrasts early and late placement more clearly than the prose.
- Figure 5 (p.8), "Response Quality Comparisons assessed by GPT4." Only useful if the note covers LLM-as-judge.

PROBLEMS:
- The paper contradicts itself on MiniGPT-4: Table 1 says 13B tuned, but the p.2 prose says the LLM is frozen. See the answer above.
- Figure 5 extracted as numbers separated from their labels. The bar values (613:521 118%, 681:669 102%, 759:759 100%, 649:652 99%, 634:660 96%, 585:704 83%, 502:698 72%) come out in the same order as the labels (GPT4, LLaMA-Adapter V2, ChatGPT, Vicuna, Bard, Alpaca, LLaMA). That reading is likely but I have not confirmed it visually. The win/tie/loss counts came out garbled ("14 2244", "507 23"). They are probably 14/22/44 for Vicuna and 50/7/23 for V2, but only the text's "50/80" is verified.
- The layer counts conflict. Sec 4.3 says "K < N − L" with "e.g., L=30". With N=32 and L=31 from the implementation details, K=1 breaks that inequality.
- Sec 5.3 credits Table 3's captioning score to "LLaMA-Adapter", while the table row says "LLaMA-Adapter V2".
- The 0.04% figure is applied loosely. Sec 4.1 uses it for the ~5M bias and scale parameters, but the abstract, intro and related work imply it covers the whole method.
- The extraction is otherwise clean. The PDF contains no embedded instructions.
